The joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ for the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\textrm {E}[X]= \dfrac{3}{4},\qquad
\textrm {E}[Y]= \dfrac{5}{12}, \qquad
\textrm {SD}[X]\approx 0.1936, \qquad
\textrm {SD}[Y]\approx 0.2444,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho = \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}[X, Y] }{\textrm {SD}[X] \cdot \textrm {SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\textrm{Cov}[X, Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\textrm {SD}[X]$ and $\textrm {SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}xy\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{x}xy\cdot 2(x+y)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{x}(2{x}^{2}y+2x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}x{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}+\frac{2}{3}{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{5}{3}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-(\frac{3}{4})(\frac{5}{12}) \\  & =\frac{1}{48}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & ≈\frac{(\frac{1}{48})}{(0.1936)\cdot (0.2444)} \\  & ≈0.44,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
